past_actions.summary: Full day at the shop — complete brake overhaul on a 2019 F-150, diagnose a rough idle on a Honda Accord, and close out two routine services. Keep the schedule tight and the quality high.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grounded but quietly unsettled. There's a low hum of unease underneath the routine — not loud enough to name, not quiet enough to ignore. Pride in today's work. Mild tension when the future comes to mind. Mostly I push the tension away by picking up a wrench.

past_actions.summary: Attend Patricia's all-hands meeting with full presence and without defensive posturing. Listen for concrete information about the Phase 2 timeline, any company pivot plans, and what leadership knows that workers don't. Take notes. Do not deflect.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grief, beginning. The specific kind that comes before acceptance — when the story you've told yourself about who you are starts to feel thin. Not collapse. Not despair. But the chest-tightening recognition that 'I fix cars, it's who I am' might be the *past* tense of a true thing rather than the present tense. There is anger underneath it — at the speed of it, at the unfairness, at having built something real with his hands only to watch the world decide hands like his matter less. But anger is still energy. He is not numb. He is not done.

past_actions.summary: Spend 90 minutes actually reading the EV certification page that has been open in the browser. Not skimming. Reading. Map his existing ASE certifications against the prerequisites for EVT (Electric Vehicle Technician) Level 2 certification. Write down on paper what he already has and what the actual gap is — not what he fears the gap is. Identify cost, time commitment, and whether the program can be done while employed.
past_actions.emotional_state: Deliberate. Slower than afraid. The grief is still there — it is sitting in the chest the way a pulled muscle reminds you it exists every time you breathe. But there is something underneath it now that is not quite hope and is not quite resolve, but is in the neighborhood. The tab is real. The reading is real. Elena deserves to know. Asking Patricia is the kind of thing a man with 23 years and a mortgage does instead of waiting for a memo.

past_actions.summary: Contact the EVT Level 2 EV certification program today and schedule the enrollment. Patricia approved the $1,400 and told me to book it. I am not waiting another day. Call the training center, confirm the next available cohort that works around my shop schedule, and register. The 60-hour program can run evenings and weekends. I am locking in a start date.

Continue EVT Level 2 evening and weekend coursework — this month focusing on high-voltage safety protocols and battery management systems. Put in the hours. Show up to class after a full day at the shop even when I'm tired. This is month two of ten. The training will not complete itself.

Continue EVT Level 2 certification retraining — month four of ten. This month the coursework moves into EV drivetrain systems, regenerative braking diagnostics, and thermal management of battery packs. The work is getting harder and more directly applicable to the EVs I will be asked to service. Show up to evening and weekend sessions. Do not skip. Do not coast. At 40% completion this is not a turning-back point — it is the point where the credential becomes visible on the horizon. The training will not complete itself and the market will not wait.

Continue EVT Level 2 certification — month five of ten. Charging infrastructure, OBD for electric drivetrains, battery fault code interpretation. 50% completion by end of this month. Have honest conversations with Sarah Kim and Miguel Hernandez — not the managed, senior-mechanic version, but the version that includes what I actually know about Rick's call and the consolidation timeline. The credential belongs to me, not to any employer. The conversations belong to the people who are asking.

reflections.reflection: Three months into this training and the world outside is validating the fear I had at tick one. The auto sector revenue index is at 79. Unemployment is climbing. The robotaxis are not a rumor anymore — they are on my street. I made the right call enrolling. I do not say that to feel good about myself. I say it because the evidence is pointing in one direction and I am now pointed in the same direction, not perpendicular to it. The hardest part is not the coursework. The hardest part is going to class tired, after a full day at the shop, when the shop itself feels like it might be contracting under me. But that tiredness is the cost of not being blindsided in month twelve.
reflections.identity_shift: The identity as 'mechanic who fixes cars' is quietly becoming 'technician who understands vehicle systems.' The hands are the same. The knowledge base is widening. I am not sure yet if I am proud of this or just resigned to it. Possibly both. What I notice is that I am no longer waiting for someone to tell me what to do — I enrolled before anyone forced me. That is different from how I handled the 2008 crisis, where I just held on and hoped. This time I moved first. That shift feels significant even if I cannot name it cleanly.
regrets: I waited too long at tick zero and tick one — those were two months of watching instead of moving. The information was available. I could have started the certification research sooner.

I have not talked to Elena honestly enough about the financial pressure. She knows I am doing the training. She does not know I am watching the sector data as closely as I am. That is a form of protection that might also be a form of avoidance.
successes: Enrolled in EVT Level 2 before being forced to — this was the right move and I made it on my own terms.
Patricia approved the shop's $1,400 contribution. I asked. She said yes. I did not assume the answer was no.
Responding to Miguel when he reaches out is the right human move. Passing forward what I know costs me nothing and might matter.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The training is at 30% after this tick. Seven months remain. Job security is still 0.77 but the sector index dropping to 79 means that number will be tested. I need to watch for any sign the shop is cutting hours or staff. If role security drops below 0.6, I need to begin networking outward — contact Angela Wright at the regional auto group, be more visible to employers who will need EV-certified technicians. For now: finish month three, stay employed, keep saving the $193 monthly delta, do not panic. The runway is 6.6 months. That is not comfortable but it is not a crisis yet.

reflections.reflection: Rick Tanner called me directly. That is the thing I keep turning over. I have worked in service lanes for 23 years and the person running the consolidation assessment called me as a peer, not as a subject. That word — tier-one — is not formal yet, but it is real. It means I am in the part of the organization that survives. That should make me feel better. It does not make me feel as much better as I expected. Because being tier-one inside a consolidation is also being inside the decision. The service technicians at whatever location closes are going to be offered transfers before any external hiring happens — I know that much from what I can piece together. Some of them I know. Some of them are people who have done this job as long as I have. I cannot change the decision. But I am not a neutral party to it either. The anxiety that spiked last tick has not resolved. It has reorganized into something more specific: I know too much to pretend I do not know things, and not enough to understand what comes next for the people who are not in tier one.
reflections.identity_shift: Something shifted in how I see myself in this organization. I went from 'a mechanic hoping to be kept' to 'a person the organization is actively accounting for.' That is a different position. It carries weight I did not fully anticipate. I am not sure whether I am more secure or less free. Possibly both. The training feels more urgent now, not because I need it to stay employed, but because I need to know that when this is over — whatever 'this' is — I am the one who decided my future, not the one who was assigned a tier.
regrets: I still have not told Elena the full picture. After Rick's call, I gave her the outline but not the weight of it. She is managing three kids and a household and I am still managing what she knows. That is a version of protection that is also a version of lying, and I know it.

I should have built a stronger relationship with Angela Wright earlier. She is running the transition program and she knows who is in what tier. That relationship at 0.40 trust is not close enough for the kind of real information I would want access to right now.
successes: Rick called me. I answered honestly. I did not perform false confidence or false fear. That was the right call and I made it.
The training is at 40% and moving to 50% this month. That progress is real and mine.
Reaching out to Miguel last tick and following through this tick is the behavior I want to model for myself — not just adaptation, but staying human while adapting.
Agreeing to have the real conversation with Sarah Kim, not the sanitized senior-mechanic version. She deserves the truth that I actually have access to, not the version that protects my authority.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Training is at 40% entering this tick, projected 50% by end of this month (month 5 of 10). Five months remain. The consolidation announcement is imminent — Patricia accelerated from two weeks to 72 hours last tick. That means by next tick I may know which location is closing and whether any of my colleagues are being transferred to my floor. I need to be ready for that to change the shop's emotional climate significantly. If transfers come, I am the senior person who receives them. That is a new responsibility I have not fully named yet. Financial: savings now approximately $36,537. Monthly delta still $193. Runway still around 6.7 months. These numbers are stable but thin. If employment status changes for any reason — consolidation goes differently than expected, sector contract accelerates — that runway tightens fast. Angela Wright at trust 0.40: if role security drops below 0.65, I need to make direct contact with her, not as a neighbor but as a professional who is positioning for the next phase. Do not wait for the floor to fall to make that move.
